findings.description: FAIL, and it is a new defect the r1 fix introduced rather than a survival of the old one. Take the two halves separately. Does part (b) close r1's hole? Yes, on all four tasks, and I re-derived each named consequence: extracted under the regex at lint-scope.sh:230 (`\[[a-z][a-z0-9 -]*(:|\])`), `[open-question: freeze-owner]` yields `[open-question:`, `[tensions: unacknowledged]` yields `[tensions:`, and neither is one of the ten rows at machine-contracts.md:67-78, so a by-hand match against that table catches both. `[memory candidate: journal]` yields `[memory candidate:`, which IS a prefix in REGISTERED_TOKENS (lint-scope.sh:26) but is not a table row -- the memory-candidate rows admit project, client, and `update existing [[...]]`, and the Journal candidate row is `[journal candidate: <generalized pattern>]` -- so matching against the table rather than against the prefix list catches T-006's named trap too. T-005's stated consequence chain is correct end to end. The r1 blocker is closed. Is the extraction procedure correct? No. Every one of the four spells the procedure out as exactly two steps -- 'strip `[[...]]` first, then read the bracketed tokens from what remains' -- over 'this fixture's tokens'. The linter's procedure has three more parts that the cited range does not show, because `check_tokens` at :218 takes a pre-extracted body as `$1`. It is called at :445 with `$body`, which is `extract_body "$file"` from :429, and `extract_body` at :208-216 drops the frontmatter, stops at `## Raw Content`, and strips HTML comments. Pass one also excludes `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` outright at :418-419. So the recipe scans four zones the linter deliberately never reads, and every one of them is populated in this repo's own correct fixtures. I ran the recipe against the linter's real pipeline over `old-only`, `mixed`, and `broken/notes/2026-03-04-unregistered-token`: the recipe reports `[extends:` and `[confirms:` (from `related: [extends::<id>]` frontmatter, the form the note template ships commented at `# related: [extends::<note-id>]`, present in 4 of 5 `mixed` notes), `[rollback]` and `[runbook]` (from flow-style `topics:`/`tags:`), and `[whatever brackets:` (from Raw Content). None is a table row; the linter reports none of them. The last one is decisive on intent: `broken/notes/2026-03-04-unregistered-token-30z5F4kx6U.md:29` exists to assert that raw content 'is deliberately allowed to contain [whatever brackets: it likes]', and machine-contracts.md says it twice -- ':158, Token scanning stops at `## Raw Content`' and the lint table's own row, 'A bracketed token in the body is absent from the grammar table.' A checker running (b) as written against a correct fixture reports unregistered tokens and fails it. This is the worker/checker mismatch you asked me to look for, and it is the r0 T-004 shape exactly: the worker is told to 'Match every inline token you write' (T-002:67, T-005:81, T-006:76) and 'inline token' is body-scoped skill vocabulary, while the checker is told to extract 'this fixture's tokens' file-wide and 'Report any token that is not a registered shape'. A worker who correctly copies `related: [extends::<id>]` from the template has written no token by their own lights and fails anyway. T-006 is the sharpest: its excerpt requires a client-root `CLAUDE.md` shaped after `inbox-to-memory/assets/claude-md/`, the linter skips `CLAUDE.md` entirely at :418-419, and `_memory.template.md` carries a bare `[memory candidate]` and `patterns-journal.template.md` a `[topic]` -- neither a table row. On attribution: the two-step gloss and the `:218-230` citation are lifted from C-9's own check field, so the words did not drift. What drifted is the subject. C-9 governs `EVALS.md`, a markdown doc with no frontmatter lists, no Raw Content section, and no CLAUDE.md, where the two steps are sufficient. The decomposition transplanted a doc-scoped procedure onto skill-format note trees without carrying over the scoping the linter applies to them. That is the decomposition's move, not the constitution's gap. Fix, one clause per task, no constitution change: scope the extraction to note bodies -- 'over each note's body, the way extract_body does at lint-scope.sh:208-216: after the frontmatter, stopping at `## Raw Content`, HTML comments removed, and skipping CLAUDE.md and README.md as pass one does at :418-419 -- then strip `[[...]]` and read what remains.' That also lands the worker and checker on the same scope.

findings.description: PASS on closure, and I reproduced r1's mechanism independently rather than taking it. Pass one at lint-scope.sh:414-432 iterates the scope's notes, records, and entries, skips CLAUDE.md and README.md, and `continue`s any file without a schema key at :421-424 -- so a bare v1 file never enters `v2_files` and pass two at :435 never sees it. A `schema: 2` file carrying `body_schema: 1` does enter, but the four body-grammar checks are gated on `! has_v1_body` at :444, so it skips those too. My probe: a copy of `old-only` with `[memory candidate: journal]`, `[open-question: freeze-owner]`, `[tensions: unacknowledged]` and `[totally made up]` appended to one note printed `v1 files: 4 / v2 files: 0 / failures: 0` and exited 0. Both statements r1 called false are gone from the four excerpts. What replaced them is accurate: T-002:67, T-003:65, T-005:81 and T-006:76 now each say the token pass 'runs only over files carrying `schema: 2`; on a v1 file it reads no tokens at all and exits 0 on a token that does not exist', which matches the code, and each ends by putting the check on the worker. The contradiction r1 named -- the excerpt asserting a lint failure one paragraph from the excerpt steering to v1 -- is resolved in the right direction: the lint claim went, the v1 steer stayed. One residual imprecision, conservative and not worth a round: 'runs only over files carrying `schema: 2`' omits the `body_schema: 1` gate, so a worker who wrote a `schema: 2` + `body_schema: 1` note and trusted the lint would be wrong. Moot, because the same sentence tells them to check by hand regardless. Also worth recording against the (a)/(b) split itself: (a) is now an instrument with no stated purpose on a v1 fixture. It still earns its place -- lint-scope.sh does check frontmatter fences, budget, key order and key domain on v2 files, and file shape generally -- but on a fully-v1 fixture 'must exit 0' is close to free, and only T-003 says so out loud.

findings.description: PASS as reasoning, with one overreach to record. T-003's (b) is stronger than its siblings for a real reason and the reason holds: its fixture cannot use the schema: 2 escape hatch, because `--tier2-extract` skips any note with a schema key (migrate-scope.sh:319-325) and a skipped note emits no extract, so every row of the Tier 2 scenario would be unfalsifiable. That is the same fact C-8's failing example turns on. So 'its exit 0 says nothing about tokens at all' is right where the siblings can only say 'the lint does not do it on a v1 fixture'. The overreach: (b) states the premise as 'this fixture is required to be v1 throughout', which nothing else in T-003 requires. The excerpt says 'Build the gradable notes as v1' (:53) and the C-8 half says 'confirm no gradable note is v2' (:34) -- both scoped to gradable notes, neither to the fixture. A worker who satisfies the excerpt exactly while planting one `schema: 2` `_memory/` record contradicts (b)'s premise, and a checker reading 'is required to' as a requirement rather than as background could fail correct work on it. Low likelihood -- the excerpt points at `old-only`, which is v1 throughout, and the task gives no motive for a v2 record -- so this is a residual, not the blocker. Two things cut the other way and are worth noting. 'v1 throughout' is close to the one-line repair r0 and r1 both asked for on the 'gradable' ambiguity, so it partly and accidentally settles that residual; it is just stated in the lint half rather than in the C-8 half where it would do the work. And T-003's C-8 invocation form is exact against the shipped usage: `migrate-scope.sh <scope-path> --tier2-extract <dir>` (migrate-scope.sh:38). The r1 residual that survives untouched is the path: `notes/` is still never named in the excerpt, and the migrator's extract sources are `"$scope"/notes/*.md`, `_memory/*/*.md`, `entries/*.md` (:319).

Each fixture task maps one behavior to one clause to one directory, so a FAIL names one thing and a rework diagnosis stays coherent -- which was the whole point of the r0 split. findings.description: Not a decomposition finding; recorded because you asked. Your reading of the mechanism is right and your conclusion about it needs narrowing. The v1 token blind spot is not a defect: machine-contracts.md:65 scopes the rule to v2 on its face ('A token shape absent from this table is a lint failure on a v2 file'), and lint-scope.sh:441-443 says why ('The body grammar checks are the ones a v1 body cannot satisfy and was never asked to'). A v1 note carrying skill tokens is out of contract by design, because v1 predates the grammar. Nothing to file there. But the same comment continues 'Links and counts stay on either way: a link that resolves nowhere is broken in any generation', and that invariant does not hold. It holds for one flavor of v1 body and not the other. A `schema: 2` file carrying `body_schema: 1` reaches pass two and gets `check_links` at :452, correctly. A file with no schema key is `continue`d out of pass one at :421-424 and never reaches :452 at all, so it gets no link check, no frontmatter check, nothing. I probed it: the identical broken wiki link, placed in the body above `## Raw Content`, fails with `link-broken` in a `mixed` v2 note and passes clean in an `old-only` bare v1 note. That is a stated intent in the code contradicted by the code, in two commands, and nothing in the contract explains why the two v1 flavors differ. Worth filing, and narrowly -- title it against the link check and the pass-one `continue`, not against token grammar, or the issue reads as a request to lint legacy notes for a vocabulary they predate. It does not touch this job: these fixtures are new authored content, their links are read directly by T-004's C-3 and C-5 checks, and C-11 backstops the tree. The non-goal at constitution.md:106 fits it exactly.
